text: Slack Technologies is a US software firm that was started in Vancouver, British Columbia, in 2009.
quote: Slack Technologies, LLC is an American software company founded in 2009 in Vancouver, British Columbia, known for its proprietary communication platform Slack.

text: Salesforce announced a $27.7 billion deal to buy Slack on December 1, 2020.
quote: On December 1, 2020, Salesforce announced its acquisition of Slack for $27.7 billion.

text: Slack Technologies traces its roots to Tiny Speck, a San Francisco startup led by Flickr co-founder Stewart Butterfield.
quote: The company goes back to the San Francisco-based startup Tiny Speck, which was headed by Stewart Butterfield, the co-founder of the photo-sharing site Flickr.

text: In October 2014 Slack Technologies took in $120 million of venture money at a $1.2 billion valuation, in a round led by Kleiner Perkins and GV.
quote: In October 2014, the company raised $120 million in venture capital with a $1.2 billion valuation led by Kleiner Perkins and GV.

text: Slack Technologies said in January 2015 that it was buying Screenhero, which specialises in voice, video and screen sharing.
quote: In January 2015, Slack announced the acquisition of Screenhero, a specialist in voice, video, and screen sharing.

text: Allen Shim became Slack Technologies' first chief financial officer, an appointment announced in early 2018.
quote: In early 2018, Slack announced the company's first CFO, Allen Shim.

text: Slack Technologies reported revenue of $400.6 million for the fiscal year ending January 31, 2019, compared with $220.5 million the year before.
quote: In the lead-up to its DPO, Slack reported that it had generated $400.6 million in revenue for the fiscal year ending January 31, 2019, up from $220.5 million in the previous year and up from $105.2 million in 2017.

text: IBM was reported in February 2020 to be rolling Slack out to its entire 350,000-person workforce, making it Slack Technologies' biggest customer so far.
quote: On February 10, 2020, it was reported that IBM will deploy Slack to all of its 350,000 employees, making IBM Slack's largest client to date.

text: Slack Technologies named its chief product officer, Rob Seaman, as interim chief executive in December 2025.
quote: In December 2025, chief product officer Rob Seaman was named interim CEO.

text: Slack Technologies took Microsoft to the European Commission in July 2020, accusing it of anticompetitive conduct.
quote: In July 2020, Slack filed a lawsuit with the European Commission accusing Microsoft of anticompetitive behavior.

text: Atlassian is based in Sydney, Australia, and focuses on collaboration tools aimed mainly at software development and project management.
quote: Atlassian () is a multinational proprietary software company headquartered in Sydney, Australia, that specialises in collaboration tools designed primarily for software development and project management.

text: Atlassian, founded in Sydney in 2002, employs more than 12,000 people in 14 countries.
quote: Founded in Sydney in 2002, the company has over 12,000 employees across 14 countries.

text: Atlassian's founders bootstrapped the business for several years, funding it with $10,000 of credit card debt.
quote: Scott Farquhar was the only one who replied, and together they founded Atlassian in 2002. They bootstrapped the company for several years, financing the startup with a $10,000 credit card debt.

text: Accel Partners put $60 million of secondary venture capital into Atlassian in July 2010.
quote: In July 2010, Atlassian raised $60 million in secondaries venture capital from Accel Partners.

text: Atlassian listed on NASDAQ under the ticker TEAM on 10 December 2015, an IPO that gave it a market capitalisation of $4.37 billion.
quote: On 10 December 2015, Atlassian made its initial public offering (IPO) on the NASDAQ stock exchange, under the symbol TEAM, putting the market capitalisation of Atlassian at $4.37 billion.

text: Atlassian announced in March 2023 that it was cutting 500 jobs, 5% of its staff.
quote: In March 2023, the firm announced layoffs of 500 employees, or 5% of its workforce.

text: Mike Cannon-Brookes became Atlassian's sole chief executive when Scott Farquhar gave up the co-CEO role at the end of August 2024.
quote: At the end of August 2024, Farquhar stepped down as co-CEO, leaving Cannon-Brookes as the sole CEO of the company.

text: Atlassian decided against a traditional sales team and built a self-service buying experience instead.
quote: Atlassian operates under the principle that "software should be bought, not sold". Instead of running a traditional sales team, they opted to build a self-service purchase experience.

text: Atlassian agreed in October 2023 to acquire the video messaging company Loom for US$975 million.
quote: In October 2023, Atlassian agreed to buy video messaging company Loom for US$975 million, with the intention to integrate Loom's technology into its services.

text: Atlassian launched Rovo, a suite of AI-based search and automation tools, in April 2024.
quote: In April 2024, Atlassian released Rovo, a set of search and automation tools that use AI.

text: Shopify has more than five million customers and handled US$292.3 billion of transactions in 2024.
quote: The company has over five million customers and processed US$292.3 billion in transactions in 2024, of which 57% was in the United States.

text: Shopify was started in 2006 by Tobias Lütke, Daniel Weinand and Scott Lake.
quote: Shopify was founded in 2006 by friends Tobias Lütke, Daniel Weinand and Scott Lake after launching Snowdevil, an online store for snowboarding equipment, in 2004.

text: Shopify Payments, introduced in August 2013 together with Stripe, lets merchants take payments without a third-party payment gateway.
quote: In August 2013, Shopify launched Shopify Payments in partnership with Stripe. Shopify Payments allows merchants to accept payments without requiring a third-party payment gateway.

text: Shopify's IPO on May 21, 2015 brought in over $131 million.
quote: Shopify went public via an initial public offering on May 21, 2015, raising more than $131 million.

text: Shopify cut about 20% of its staff in May 2023 and sold its in-house logistics arm, Shopify Logistics, to Flexport.
quote: In May 2023, Shopify laid off approximately 20% of its workforce and sold Shopify Logistics, its in-house logistics arm, to Flexport, which subsequently became the preferred logistics partner for the e-commerce platform.

text: Shopify announced on May 5, 2022 that it would buy the San Francisco fulfilment startup Deliverr for US$2.1 billion in cash and stock.
quote: On May 5, 2022, Shopify announced its acquisition of Deliverr, a San Francisco, California-based ecommerce fulfilment startup, for US$2.1 billion in cash and stock.

text: Shopify reported full-year 2025 revenue of $11.56 billion, 30% above 2024.
quote: In February 2026, Shopify reported Q4 2025 revenue of $3.67 billion, a 31% year-over-year increase, and full-year 2025 revenue of $11.56 billion, up 30% from 2024, driven by growth in B2B sales and expanded AI commerce tools.

text: Shopify confirmed in September 2020 that it had suffered a data breach in which customer data belonging to as many as 200 merchants was stolen.
quote: In September 2020, Shopify confirmed a data breach in which customer data for up to 200 merchants was stolen.

text: A group of publishers including Pearson Education and McGraw Hill sued Shopify in December 2021, alleging it had not taken down listings and stores selling pirated copies of their books and learning materials.
quote: In December 2021, a group of publishers including; Pearson Education Inc., Macmillan Learning, Cengage Learning, Inc., Elsevier Inc., and McGraw Hill sued Shopify, claiming that it had failed to remove listings and stores selling pirated copies of their books and learning materials.

text: Shopify said in 2024 that its Shop Pay checkout had more than 150 million users globally.
quote: In 2024, Shopify reported that Shop Pay had over 150 million users worldwide.

text: Twilio is a US cloud communications company headquartered in San Francisco, California.
quote: Twilio Inc. is an American cloud communications company based in San Francisco, California

text: Twilio was set up in 2008 by Jeff Lawson, Evan Cooke and John Wolthuis, all University of Michigan graduates.
quote: Twilio was founded in 2008 by University of Michigan graduates Jeff Lawson, Evan Cooke, and John Wolthuis and was based initially in Seattle, Washington, and San Francisco, California.

text: Twilio Voice, a cloud-hosted API for placing and receiving phone calls, went live on November 20, 2008.
quote: On November 20, 2008, the company launched Twilio Voice, an API to make and receive phone calls completely hosted in the cloud.

text: Twilio closed a $130 million Series E in July 2015 whose backers included Fidelity, T Rowe Price, Amazon and Salesforce.
quote: In July 2015, Twilio raised a $130 million Series E from Fidelity, T Rowe Price, Altimeter Capital Management, and Arrowpoint Partners, in addition to Amazon and Salesforce.

text: Twilio went public on the New York Stock Exchange on June 23, 2016, and its shares gained 92% on the first day.
quote: Twilio's initial public offering took place on the New York Stock Exchange on June 23, 2016, with a 92% increase in share price on the first day.

text: Twilio let go 11% of its employees in September 2022.
quote: In September 2022, Twilio laid off 11% of its workforce.

text: Khozema Shipchandler took over as Twilio's chief executive after founder Jeff Lawson stepped down as CEO and left the board in January 2024.
quote: Twilio founder Jeff Lawson stepped down as CEO and board member in January 2024 and was succeeded by Khozema Shipchandler.

text: Twilio announced in October 2018 a $2 billion deal to buy SendGrid, a Denver-based platform for transactional and marketing email.
quote: In October 2018 Twilio announced it was acquiring SendGrid, a Denver, Colorado-based customer communication platform for transactional and marketing email, for $2 billion.

text: Twilio's communication infrastructure is hosted on Amazon Web Services.
quote: Twilio uses Amazon Web Services to host its communication infrastructure via APIs.

text: In a July 2024 breach, the ShinyHunters hacking group exploited an unsecured Twilio API to obtain phone numbers of more than 33 million Authy users.
quote: In a July 2024 data breach, the ShinyHunters hacker group used an unsecured Twilio API to acquire the phone numbers of over 33 million Authy users.

text: Dropbox was started in 2007 by two MIT students, Drew Houston and Arash Ferdowsi, with early money from the seed accelerator Y Combinator.
quote: Dropbox was founded in 2007 by MIT students Drew Houston and Arash Ferdowsi as a startup company, with initial funding from seed accelerator Y Combinator.

text: The Dropbox Basic tier comes with two gigabytes of storage at no charge.
quote: Dropbox Basic users are given two gigabytes of free storage space.

text: Dropbox bought the e-signature company HelloSign in January 2019 for a reported $230 million, reportedly its biggest acquisition up to that point.
quote: In January 2019, Dropbox acquired e-signature company HelloSign. The acquisition was reported to be Dropbox's largest to date, at a reported $230 million.

text: Dropbox CEO Houston announced 315 job cuts in January 2021, roughly 11 percent of the workforce at that time.
quote: In January 2021, Dropbox CEO Houston announced the layoff of 315 employees, which was approximately 11 percent of the workforce at the time.

text: Dropbox said in May 2026 that co-founder Drew Houston would give up the chief executive post and become executive chairman.
quote: In May 2026, Dropbox announced that co-founder Drew Houston will step down from the role of chief executive officer to assume the role of executive chairman.

text: Sequoia Capital led Dropbox's $6 million Series A in October 2008, and Accel also took part.
quote: In October 2008, Dropbox raised a $6 million Series A round led by Sequoia Capital with participation from Accel.

text: Dropbox shares climbed 42 percent to $29.89 on their first trading day, March 23, 2018.
quote: Dropbox's stock rose 42 percent to $29.89 in its first day of trading on March 23, 2018.

text: Dropbox's Smart Sync, introduced in January 2017 for Business and Enterprise customers, lets Windows and macOS users see every file in the Dropbox folder while downloading only specific files on demand.
quote: In January 2017, Dropbox introduced "Smart Sync" for Business and Enterprise customers, a feature that lets Windows and macOS users see all files in the Dropbox folder, but only download specific files on-demand.

text: Dropbox synchronizes over SSL and stores data using AES-256 encryption.
quote: Dropbox uses SSL transfers for synchronization and stores the data via Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)-256 encryption.

text: Dropbox opened its first office outside the United States in Dublin, Ireland, in December 2012.
quote: In December 2012, Dropbox set up an office in Dublin, Ireland, its first office outside the United States.

text: Zoom Communications was established in 2011 by Eric Yuan, who had been an engineer and executive at Cisco.
quote: The company was founded in 2011 by Eric Yuan, a former Cisco engineer and executive.

text: Zoom Communications is a US communications technology company with headquarters in San Jose, California.
quote: is an American communications technology company headquartered in San Jose, California, United States.

text: Stanford University became Zoom Communications' first customer in November 2012.
quote: In November 2012, the company signed Stanford University as its first customer.

text: Zoom Communications reached unicorn status in January 2017, when Sequoia Capital provided US$100 million of Series D funding at a US$1 billion valuation.
quote: In January 2017, the company raised US$100 million in Series D funding from Sequoia Capital at a US$1 billion valuation, making it a unicorn.

text: Zoom Communications went public through an IPO on April 18, 2019 and trades on Nasdaq under the ticker ZM.
quote: On April 18, 2019, the company became a public company via an initial public offering; since then, it has been listed on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ZM.

text: Shareholders of the contact center company Five9 rejected Zoom's $14.7 billion bid to acquire it.
quote: Zoom's attempt to acquire contact center company Five9 for $14.7 billion in September of that year was turned down by Five9's shareholders.

text: Zoom said in February 2023 that it would shed 15 percent of its staff, around 1,300 people, blaming unsustainable growth after scaling quickly to meet pandemic demand.
quote: Zoom announced that it would cut its workforce by 15 percent, or about 1,300 employees, in February 2023, citing unsustainable growth following rapid scaling to manage the demand of the pandemic.

text: Zoom Video Communications, Inc. changed its name to Zoom Communications, Inc. in November 2024, removing 'Video' from the name.
quote: In November 2024, Zoom Video Communications, Inc. rebranded as Zoom Communications, Inc., dropping 'Video' from its name

text: Zoom agreed to an $85 million settlement of a class action over its alleged sharing of data with Facebook, Linkedin and Google.
quote: Zoom agreed to pay $85 million to settle a class action lawsuit over the company's alleged sharing of data with Facebook, Linkedin, and Google that year.

text: On April 1, 2020, Zoom announced it would pause new feature releases for 90 days so it could concentrate on fixing privacy and security problems.
quote: On April 1, 2020, Zoom announced a 90-day freeze on releasing new features, to focus on fixing privacy and security issues on Zoom.
